guitar.guitaristsText: Mick Ronson / Carlos Alomar / Earl Slick
guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul (Ronson) / Fender Stratocaster / Telecaster
guitar.notes: Bowie used many different guitarists across eras with no single signature instrument tied to Bowie himself; medium is appropriate given Ronson's well-known Les Paul.

tone.target: bright glam-rock crunch with biting mids
tone.profile: bright glam-rock crunch with biting mids
tone.summary: A tight signal chain using a British-style overdrive and amp model (UK 45) combined with a classic 4x12 cabinet to achieve bright, crunchy glam-rock tones suitable for staccato riffs.
corrections: replace mid-scooped overdrive with biting crunch
keep fuzz only as slight grit, not main gain

rig.name: David Bowie - Suffragette City - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain passages and staccato picking.
Provide biting mid-range crunch and slight grit without sounding like modern scooped distortion.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is chosen for its classic, midrange-focused character, mimicking the Plexi/Marshall tone required. A dedicated Tube Screamer model would be ideal but is not available.

blocks.purpose: Optional accenting and vocal flair typical of glam rock.
Add slight fuzz grit and bite for the 'Suffragette City' texture without overwhelming the main crunch.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is used sparingly to provide a gritty edge, fulfilling the 'slight fuzz grit' requirement. A dedicated low-gain boost or light overdrive would be better, but this provides necessary bite.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British Plexi/Marshall sound required for glam rock.
Provide the classic British 4x12 cabinet sound.
Boost the upper mids and biting frequencies to achieve the 'bright' tone.
Add subtle rhythmic depth and separation to the staccato riffs.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a more authentic British glam-rock sound.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Plexi/Marshall character and mid-range bite.
